427	def _required_stream_requests(
428	    *,
429	    evidence_root: Path,
430	    required_paths: tuple[str, ...],
431	    index: Any,
432	    offset: Any,
433	    max_chunks: Any = MAX_CODEX_REQUIRED_READ_CHUNKS,
434	    max_bytes: Any = SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES,
435	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
436	    """Derive the exact chunks emitted by one parent-owned required read."""
437	    if (
438	        not isinstance(index, int)
439	        or isinstance(index, bool)
440	        or not isinstance(offset, int)
441	        or isinstance(offset, bool)
442	        or index < 0
443	        or index >= len(required_paths)
444	        or offset < 0
445	        or not isinstance(max_chunks, int)
446	        or isinstance(max_chunks, bool)
447	        or max_chunks < 1
448	        or max_chunks > MAX_CODEX_REQUIRED_READ_CHUNKS
449	        or not isinstance(max_bytes, int)
450	        or isinstance(max_bytes, bool)
451	        or max_bytes < 1
452	        or max_bytes > SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES
453	    ):
454	        return []
455	    requests: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
456	    while index < len(required_paths) and len(requests) < max_chunks:
457	        rel_path = required_paths[index]
458	        data = (evidence_root / rel_path).read_bytes()
459	        if offset > len(data):
460	            return []
461	        end = min(len(data), offset + max_bytes)
462	        while end > offset:
463	            try:
464	                data[offset:end].decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
465	                break
466	            except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
467	                if exc.reason != "unexpected end of data":
468	                    return []
469	                end -= 1
470	        requests.append(
471	            {
472	                "path": rel_path,
473	                "offset": offset,
474	                "max_bytes": max_bytes,
475	            }
476	        )
477	        if end == len(data):
478	            index += 1
479	            offset = 0
480	        elif end > offset:
481	            offset = end
482	        else:
483	            return []
484	    return requests

487	def _all_required_requests(
488	    *, evidence_root: Path, required_paths: tuple[str, ...]
489	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
490	    """Derive every bounded chunk for one all-required sealed read."""
491	    total_bytes = sum((evidence_root / rel_path).stat().st_size for rel_path in required_paths)
492	    if total_bytes > MAX_CODEX_REQUIRED_TOTAL_BYTES:
493	        return []
494	    requests: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
495	    for rel_path in required_paths:
496	        data = (evidence_root / rel_path).read_bytes()
497	        offset = 0
498	        while True:
499	            end = min(len(data), offset + SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES)
500	            while end > offset:
501	                try:
502	                    data[offset:end].decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
503	                    break
504	                except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
505	                    if exc.reason != "unexpected end of data":
506	                        return []
507	                    end -= 1
508	            requests.append(
509	                {
510	                    "path": rel_path,
511	                    "offset": offset,
512	                    "max_bytes": SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES,
513	                }
514	            )
515	            if len(requests) > MAX_CODEX_REQUIRED_ALL_CHUNKS:
516	                return []
517	            if end == len(data):
518	                break
519	            if end <= offset:
520	                return []
521	            offset = end
522	    return requests

525	def _codex_sealed_read_requests(
526	    call: dict[str, Any], *, evidence_root: Path, required_paths: tuple[str, ...]
527	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
528	    """Return trace-bound sealed reads, including strict Codex JS transports."""
529	    name = str(call.get("name") or "").lower()
530	    arguments = call.get("arguments")
531	    if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
532	        return []
533	    if (
534	        name == "read_file"
535	        or name.endswith("sealed_review__read_file")
536	        or name.endswith("sealed_review.read_file")
537	        or name.endswith("sealed_review_read_file")
538	    ):
539	        request = _validated_codex_read_request(
540	            raw_path=arguments.get("path"),
541	            offset=arguments.get("offset", 0),
542	            max_bytes=arguments.get("max_bytes", SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES),
543	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
544	        )
545	        return [request] if request is not None else []
546	    if (
547	        name == "read_required"
548	        or name.endswith("sealed_review__read_required")
549	        or name.endswith("sealed_review.read_required")
550	        or name.endswith("sealed_review_read_required")
551	    ):
552	        return _required_stream_requests(
553	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
554	            required_paths=required_paths,
555	            index=arguments.get("index", 0),
556	            offset=arguments.get("offset", 0),
557	            max_chunks=arguments.get(
558	                "max_chunks", MAX_CODEX_REQUIRED_READ_CHUNKS
559	            ),
560	            max_bytes=arguments.get("max_bytes", SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES),
561	        )
562	    if name == "read_required_all" or name.endswith(
563	        "sealed_review__read_required_all"
564	    ) or name.endswith("sealed_review.read_required_all") or name.endswith(
565	        "sealed_review_read_required_all"
566	    ):
567	        return _all_required_requests(
568	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
569	            required_paths=required_paths,
570	        )
571	    if name != "exec":
572	        return []
573	    raw = arguments.get("_raw")
574	    if not isinstance(raw, str) or len(raw) > MAX_CODEX_SEALED_READ_EXEC_CHARS:
575	        return []
576	    match = _CODEX_SEALED_READ_EXEC_RE.fullmatch(raw)
577	    if match is not None:
578	        try:
579	            raw_path = json.loads(match.group("path"))
580	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
581	            return []
582	        request = _validated_codex_read_request(
583	            raw_path=raw_path,
584	            offset=int(match.group("offset")),
585	            max_bytes=int(match.group("max_bytes")),
586	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
587	        )
588	        return [request] if request is not None else []
589	    required_match = _CODEX_SEALED_REQUIRED_READ_RE.fullmatch(raw)
590	    if required_match is not None:
591	        return _required_stream_requests(
592	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
593	            required_paths=required_paths,
594	            index=int(required_match.group("index")),
595	            offset=int(required_match.group("offset")),
596	        )
597	    if _CODEX_SEALED_REQUIRED_ALL_RE.fullmatch(raw) is not None:
598	        return _all_required_requests(
599	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
600	            required_paths=required_paths,
601	        )
602	    batch_match = _CODEX_SEALED_READ_BATCH_RE.fullmatch(raw)
603	    if batch_match is None:
604	        return []
605	    try:
606	        raw_requests = json.loads(batch_match.group("requests"))
607	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
608	        return []
609	    if (
610	        not isinstance(raw_requests, list)
611	        or not raw_requests
612	        or len(raw_requests) > MAX_CODEX_SEALED_READ_BATCH
613	    ):
614	        return []
615	    requests: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
616	    identities: set[tuple[str, int]] = set()
617	    for item in raw_requests:
618	        if not isinstance(item, list) or len(item) != 2:
619	            return []
620	        request = _validated_codex_read_request(
621	            raw_path=item[0],
622	            offset=item[1],
623	            max_bytes=SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES,
624	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
625	        )
626	        if request is None:
627	            return []
628	        identity = (request["path"], request["offset"])
629	        if identity in identities:
630	            return []
631	        identities.add(identity)
632	        requests.append(request)
633	    return requests

636	def _intervals_cover(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]], *, size: int) -> bool:
637	    if size == 0:
638	        return bool(intervals)
639	    cursor = 0
640	    for start, end in sorted(intervals):
641	        if start > cursor:
642	            return False
643	        cursor = max(cursor, end)
644	        if cursor >= size:
645	            return True
646	    return False

649	def _verify_codex_review_reads(
650	    tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]],
651	    *,
652	    evidence_root: Path,
653	    required_paths: tuple[str, ...],
654	) -> dict[str, Any]:
655	    _validate_review_read_sizes(evidence_root, required_paths)
656	    file_bytes = {path: (evidence_root / path).read_bytes() for path in required_paths}
657	    coverage: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {path: [] for path in required_paths}
658	    delivered_bytes: dict[str, int] = {path: 0 for path in required_paths}
659	    empty_reads: set[str] = set()
660	    for call in tool_calls:
661	        if not _tool_result_succeeded(call):
662	            continue
663	        requests = _codex_sealed_read_requests(
664	            call,
665	            evidence_root=evidence_root,
666	            required_paths=required_paths,
667	        )
668	        if not requests and str(call.get("name") or ""):
669	            continue
670	        by_identity = {
671	            (request["path"], request["offset"]): request
672	            for request in requests
673	            if request["path"] in coverage
674	        }
675	        for payload in _mcp_chunk_payloads(call.get("result")):
676	            identity = (payload.get("path"), payload.get("offset"))
677	            request = by_identity.get(identity)
678	            # ``name`` is an unstable optional ACP field. OpenCode currently
679	            # emits the standard human-readable ``title`` plus rawInput and
680	            # rawOutput, so authenticate a name-less call from the sealed
681	            # payload itself. The payload remains bound to the parent snapshot
682	            # by exact path, full-file digest, chunk digest, offsets, content,
683	            # and the public chunk cap; title text alone never grants coverage.
684	            if request is None and not str(call.get("name") or ""):
685	                payload_path = payload.get("path")
686	                payload_offset = payload.get("offset")
687	                if (
688	                    payload_path in coverage
689	                    and isinstance(payload_offset, int)
690	                    and not isinstance(payload_offset, bool)
691	                    and payload_offset >= 0
692	                ):
693	                    request = {
694	                        "path": payload_path,
695	                        "offset": payload_offset,
696	                        "max_bytes": SEALED_READ_CHUNK_BYTES,
697	                    }
698	            if request is None:
699	                continue
700	            rel_path = request["path"]
701	            data = file_bytes[rel_path]
702	            offset = payload.get("offset")
703	            chunk_bytes = payload.get("chunk_bytes")
704	            next_offset = payload.get("next_offset")
705	            total_bytes = payload.get("total_bytes")
706	            content = payload.get("content")
707	            if (
708	                not isinstance(offset, int)
709	                or isinstance(offset, bool)
710	                or not isinstance(chunk_bytes, int)
711	                or isinstance(chunk_bytes, bool)
712	                or not isinstance(next_offset, int)
713	                or isinstance(next_offset, bool)
714	                or not isinstance(total_bytes, int)
715	                or isinstance(total_bytes, bool)
716	                or not isinstance(content, str)
717	                or offset != request["offset"]
718	                or chunk_bytes < 0
719	                or chunk_bytes > request["max_bytes"]
720	                or next_offset != offset + chunk_bytes
721	                or total_bytes != len(data)
722	                or next_offset > total_bytes
723	            ):
724	                continue
725	            encoded = content.encode("utf-8")
726	            if (
727	                len(encoded) != chunk_bytes
728	                or data[offset:next_offset] != encoded
729	                or payload.get("sha256") != hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
730	                or payload.get("chunk_sha256") != hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()
731	                or payload.get("eof") is not (next_offset == total_bytes)
732	            ):
733	                continue
734	            if total_bytes == 0:
735	                empty_reads.add(rel_path)
736	                coverage[rel_path].append((0, 0))
737	            elif chunk_bytes:
738	                coverage[rel_path].append((offset, next_offset))
739	            delivered_bytes[rel_path] += chunk_bytes
740	
741	    missing = [
742	        path
743	        for path, intervals in coverage.items()
744	        if not (_intervals_cover(intervals, size=(evidence_root / path).stat().st_size) or path in empty_reads)
745	    ]
746	    if missing:
747	        raise ReviewWorktreeError("review_evidence_reads_incomplete:" + ",".join(missing))
748	    unique_bytes = sum(len(file_bytes[path]) for path in required_paths)
749	    total_delivered_bytes = sum(delivered_bytes.values())
750	    return {
751	        "mode": "hash_bound_byte_chunks",
752	        "covered_paths": list(required_paths),
753	        "covered_path_count": len(required_paths),
754	        "bytes_delivered_per_artifact": delivered_bytes,
755	        "unique_evidence_bytes": unique_bytes,
756	        "total_delivered_bytes": total_delivered_bytes,
757	        "duplicate_delivered_bytes": max(0, total_delivered_bytes - unique_bytes),
758	    }

761	def _verify_builtin_review_reads(
762	    tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]],
763	    *,
764	    evidence_root: Path,
765	    required_paths: tuple[str, ...],
766	) -> dict[str, Any]:
767	    _validate_review_read_sizes(evidence_root, required_paths)
768	    file_lines: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
769	    coverage: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {}
770	    empty_reads: set[str] = set()
771	    for rel_path in required_paths:
772	        data = (evidence_root / rel_path).read_bytes()
773	        try:
774	            text = data.decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
775	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
776	            raise ReviewWorktreeError(f"review_evidence_not_utf8:{rel_path}") from exc
777	        lines_with_ends = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
778	        if any(len(line.encode("utf-8")) > MAX_BUILTIN_READ_LINE_BYTES for line in lines_with_ends):
779	            raise ReviewWorktreeError(f"review_evidence_split_required:long_line:{rel_path}")
780	        file_lines[rel_path] = text.splitlines()
781	        coverage[rel_path] = []
782	
783	    for call in tool_calls:
784	        name = str(call.get("name") or "").lower()
785	        if name not in {"read", "read_file"} and not name.endswith("__read"):
786	            continue
787	        if not _tool_result_succeeded(call):
788	            continue
789	        arguments = call.get("arguments")
790	        if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
791	            continue
792	        raw_path = arguments.get("file_path") or arguments.get("path")
793	        rel_path = _normalized_read_path(raw_path, evidence_root=evidence_root)
794	        if rel_path not in coverage:
795	            continue
796	        offset = arguments.get("offset", 1)
797	        limit = arguments.get("limit", MAX_BUILTIN_READ_LINES)
798	        if (
799	            not isinstance(offset, int)
800	            or isinstance(offset, bool)
801	            or not isinstance(limit, int)
802	            or isinstance(limit, bool)
803	            or offset < 0
804	            or limit < 1
805	            or limit > MAX_BUILTIN_READ_LINES
806	        ):
807	            continue
808	        start = max(1, offset)
809	        lines = file_lines[rel_path]
810	        total = len(lines)
811	        if total == 0:
812	            empty_reads.add(rel_path)
813	            coverage[rel_path].append((0, 0))

1	"""Canonical cross-family reviewer resolver for code-review closeout.
2	
3	Family follows the MODEL, not the harness or CLI name — the same underlying
4	model reachable through different tooling (native CLI, hermes, a `-tools`
5	V7 seat) always resolves to the same family, so an author can't dodge the
6	cross-family requirement by switching harness. Domain and data-egress
7	exclusions are fail-closed: an unspecified or non-matching policy excludes
8	a gated candidate, it does not admit it. Missing lane-health data is fail-open
9	(no signal ≠ unhealthy, matching ``scripts/api/lane_health.py``'s convention),
10	but an explicitly unhealthy route is unavailable. Degraded and near-capacity
11	signals only break ties among candidates in the same quality rung; they never
12	demote a model into a lower-quality rung.
13	
14	The model inventory, candidate routes, and risk ladders are loaded from the
15	versioned ``scripts/config/model_catalog.yaml`` catalog at import time
16	(``REVIEW_CANDIDATES`` / ``REVIEW_LADDERS`` via ``_catalog_candidate`` /
17	``_catalog_ladder``). **Policy changes to ladder order or formal CF seats are
18	YAML edits** — this module must not hard-code a second ladder. As of the
19	fleet-comms practical-CF pin (#5512): ``critical`` keeps authority-first
20	(Sol/Fable/Opus); ``high|medium|low`` walk practical seats (Terra, Sonnet 5,
21	Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok native + Cursor-explicit ``grok-4.5`` fallback, …).
22	Its separate freshness lint forces a provider/CLI/source review every 30 days
23	without making a stale catalog an operational outage at runtime.
24	"""
25

44	def resolve_family(seat_or_model: str) -> str:
45	    """Resolve a seat/CLI-alias/model-id string to its model family.
46	
47	    Returns ``"unknown"`` for anything unrecognized — callers must not treat
48	    unknown as any specific family (including the author's own), since that
49	    would either wrongly admit or wrongly exclude a candidate.
50	    """
51	    normalized = (seat_or_model or "").strip().lower()
52	    if not normalized:
53	        return "unknown"
54	
55	    canonical = normalize_seat(normalized) or normalized
56	
57	    if canonical.endswith("-tools"):
58	        base = tools_writer_runtime_agent(canonical)
59	        canonical = base
60	
61	    family = model_families.normalize_family(canonical)
62	    if family in {model_families.Family.UNKNOWN, model_families.Family.FIXTURE}:
63	        return UNKNOWN_AUTHOR_FAMILY
64	    return family.value
65	
66	
67	# --- ambiguous-harness / fail-closed author identity --------------------------
68	
69	# Harnesses that route to more than one underlying model family depending on
70	# per-session configuration — the harness name alone is NOT a model family.
71	# Cursor is multi-model (a session may run GPT, Claude, or another model
72	# underneath); resolving it to a synthetic "cursor" family would let an
73	# author dodge the cross-family requirement whenever the real underlying
74	# model happens to collide with whatever the ladder picks.
75	AMBIGUOUS_HARNESS_SEATS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"cursor", "cursor-tools"})
76	
77	# Concrete model-vendor families a caller may assert via an explicit
78	# ``author_family`` override. Deliberately excludes harness pseudo-families
79	# (nothing routes to "cursor" as if it were a vendor) and the fail-closed
80	# sentinels below — an override must name a real family or be rejected.
81	_VALID_CONCRETE_FAMILIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
82	    family.value
83	    for family in model_families.Family
84	    if family not in {model_families.Family.UNKNOWN, model_families.Family.FIXTURE}
85	)
86	
87	# Fail-closed author-identity outcomes: none of these is a real model family,
88	# and a caller must never treat one as matching (or not matching) any
89	# candidate's family — resolve_reviewer refuses to select a formal reviewer
90	# for any of them.
91	UNKNOWN_AUTHOR_FAMILY = "unknown"
92	AMBIGUOUS_AUTHOR_FAMILY = "ambiguous"
93	CONFLICTING_AUTHOR_FAMILY = "conflict"
94	UNRESOLVED_AUTHOR_FAMILIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
95	    {UNKNOWN_AUTHOR_FAMILY, AMBIGUOUS_AUTHOR_FAMILY, CONFLICTING_AUTHOR_FAMILY}
96	)

99	def resolve_author_family(author_model: str, author_family: str | None = None) -> str:
100	    """Resolve the author's model family, failing closed for ambiguous harnesses.
101	
102	    ``author_model`` is either a concrete seat/model id (resolved exactly as
103	    :func:`resolve_family` always has), or a ``"<harness>:<concrete-model>"``
104	    composite for a multi-model harness (e.g. ``"cursor:gpt-5.6-sol"``,
105	    ``"cursor:claude-opus-4-8"``) that disambiguates which model that harness
106	    session actually ran. ``author_family`` is an optional explicit,
107	    caller-asserted family (e.g. from session logs) used to corroborate or,
108	    for a bare ambiguous-harness identity with no embedded model, to supply
109	    the disambiguation on its own.
110	
111	    Returns a concrete family string, or one of the fail-closed sentinels:
112	
113	    - ``"unknown"`` — no usable identity signal at all.
114	    - ``"ambiguous"`` — a multi-model harness with no concrete model and no
115	      valid override to disambiguate it.
116	    - ``"conflict"`` — the embedded/resolved model family and an explicit
117	      ``author_family`` override disagree.
118	
119	    Callers (:func:`resolve_reviewer`) must never select a formal reviewer
120	    against a fail-closed sentinel — an unresolved author identity is not
121	    evidence that a candidate is (or isn't) the same family.
122	    """
123	    normalized = (author_model or "").strip().lower()
124	    override = (author_family or "").strip().lower() or None
125	    if override is not None and override not in _VALID_CONCRETE_FAMILIES:
126	        override = None  # an invalid/unrecognized override does not count as validated
127	
128	    harness_token, sep, embedded = normalized.partition(":")
129	    if sep and harness_token in AMBIGUOUS_HARNESS_SEATS and embedded.strip():
130	        resolved = resolve_family(embedded.strip())
131	    elif normalized in AMBIGUOUS_HARNESS_SEATS or (normalize_seat(normalized) or "") in AMBIGUOUS_HARNESS_SEATS:
132	        resolved = None  # bare ambiguous harness, no embedded concrete model
133	    else:
134	        resolved = resolve_family(normalized)
135	
136	    if resolved is None:
137	        # Bare ambiguous harness: only a validated override can disambiguate it.
138	        return override if override else AMBIGUOUS_AUTHOR_FAMILY
139	    if resolved == "unknown":
140	        return override if override else UNKNOWN_AUTHOR_FAMILY
141	    if override and override != resolved:
142	        return CONFLICTING_AUTHOR_FAMILY
143	    return resolved

314	        raise ValueError(f"{label} has unsupported health status {value!r}; expected one of {sorted(_HEALTH_ALIASES)}")
315	    return _HEALTH_ALIASES[token]

318	def normalize_routing_snapshot(snapshot: Mapping[str, object] | None) -> dict[str, str]:
319	    """Accept either a flat route->status map or `/api/state/routing-budget`."""
320	    if not snapshot:
321	        return {}
322	    if not isinstance(snapshot, Mapping):
323	        raise ValueError("routing snapshot must be a mapping")
324	    if "agents" not in snapshot:
325	        normalized_flat: dict[str, str] = {}
326	        for route, status in snapshot.items():
327	            normalized_status = _normalize_health_status(status, label=str(route))
328	            if normalized_status is not None:
329	                normalized_flat[str(route)] = normalized_status
330	        return normalized_flat
331	
332	    agents = snapshot.get("agents")
333	    if not isinstance(agents, Mapping):
334	        raise ValueError("routing snapshot agents must be a mapping")
335	    normalized: dict[str, str] = {}
336	    for route, raw in agents.items():
337	        if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
338	            raise ValueError(f"routing snapshot agents.{route} must be a mapping")
339	        health = raw.get("health")
340	        if isinstance(health, Mapping) and health.get("healthy") is False:
341	            normalized[str(route)] = "unhealthy"
342	            continue
343	        status = raw.get("status")
344	        if status is None and isinstance(health, Mapping) and health.get("healthy") is True:
345	            normalized[str(route)] = "healthy"
346	            continue
347	        if status is None:
348	            # A transaction-local scheduler snapshot may carry only pressure
349	            # counters. Health remains fail-open when it is genuinely absent.
350	            continue
351	        normalized_status = _normalize_health_status(status, label=f"agents.{route}")
352	        if normalized_status is not None:
353	            normalized[str(route)] = normalized_status
354	    return normalized

489	def _hard_exclusion_reason(candidate: ReviewerCandidate, inputs: ResolverInputs) -> str | None:
490	    """Non-family exclusions: cost policy, domain carve-out, data-egress
491	    (fail-closed), missing required capability. Family/advisory handling is
492	    the caller's job — this only covers filters that apply regardless."""
493	    if candidate.always_excluded_reason:
494	        return candidate.always_excluded_reason
495	    if inputs.formal_review:
496	        if not candidate.formal_review_eligible:
497	            return candidate.formal_review_exclusion_reason or (
498	                "formal-review transport is not eligible for a sealed cross-family gate"
499	            )
500	        if not candidate.endpoint or candidate.endpoint != candidate.route:
501	            return "sealed endpoint identity is missing or does not match the candidate route"
502	        if not candidate.participant or not candidate.sealed_executable:
503	            return "sealed ACP participant or review executable identity is missing"
504	        if candidate.adapter_transport != "acp":
505	            return "formal-review candidate is not bound to the ACP adapter transport"
506	        if candidate.sealed_executable != _SEALED_REVIEW_EXECUTABLE:
507	            return "candidate is not bound to the sealed review-pr ACP executable"
508	        if candidate.participant not in ACPX_SUPPORTED_PARTICIPANTS:
509	            return "candidate ACP participant is not enabled by the runner-owned adapter registry"
510	        if ACPX_PARTICIPANT_CATALOG_TRANSPORTS.get(candidate.participant) != candidate.catalog_transport:
511	            return "candidate catalog transport does not match its runner-owned ACP participant"
512	        if candidate.transport != candidate.catalog_transport:
513	            return "candidate transport does not match its ACPX catalog transport"
514	        if (
515	            not candidate.quota_bucket
516	            or not candidate.credential_bucket
517	            or candidate.quota_limit < 1
518	            or candidate.credential_limit < 1
519	            or candidate.capacity_weight <= 0
520	        ):
521	            return "formal-review capacity configuration is invalid"
522	    review_profile = inputs.review_profile.strip().casefold()
523	    if review_profile not in candidate.review_profiles:
524	        return (
525	            f"review profile exclusion: {candidate.name} supports "
526	            f"{sorted(candidate.review_profiles)}, got {inputs.review_profile!r}"
527	        )
528	    if inputs.domain in candidate.domain_excluded_from:
529	        return f"hard domain exclusion: {candidate.name} is excluded from {inputs.domain!r} review"
530	    if (
531	        candidate.requires_data_egress_policy is not None
532	        and inputs.data_egress_policy != candidate.requires_data_egress_policy
533	    ):
534	        return (
535	            f"data-egress policy fail-closed: {candidate.name} requires "
536	            f"data_egress_policy={candidate.requires_data_egress_policy!r}, "
537	            f"got {inputs.data_egress_policy!r}"
538	        )
539	    missing = inputs.required_capabilities - candidate.capabilities
540	    if missing:
541	        return f"missing required capabilities: {sorted(missing)}"
542	    if inputs.isolation_required and "isolation" not in candidate.capabilities:
543	        return "isolation required but candidate does not support process isolation"
544	    return None

547	def _suitability_rank(candidate: ReviewerCandidate, inputs: ResolverInputs) -> int | None:
548	    """Return catalog-backed semantic suitability, or fail closed.
549	
550	    This intentionally precedes quality and all resource pressure. It is not a
551	    probabilistic score and has no rotation term: a lower integer means a
552	    better profile/risk role match among candidates that passed hard gates.
553	    """
554	    requested_role = (inputs.requested_role or "").strip()
555	    if requested_role:
556	        return 0 if requested_role in candidate.model_roles else None
557	    profile = inputs.review_profile.strip().casefold()
558	    risk = inputs.risk.strip().casefold()
559	    try:
560	        ordered_roles = _SCHEDULER_POLICY["profile_risk_role_order"][profile][risk]
561	    except (KeyError, TypeError):
562	        return None
563	    for rank, role in enumerate(ordered_roles):
564	        if role in candidate.model_roles:
565	            return rank
566	    return None

569	def evaluate_candidate(
570	    candidate: ReviewerCandidate,
571	    inputs: ResolverInputs,
572	    *,
573	    author_family: str | None = None,
574	) -> CandidateResult:
575	    """Evaluate one candidate against ``inputs`` independent of ladder position.
576	
577	    Exposed directly (not just via :func:`resolve_reviewer`) so domain and
578	    data-egress fail-closed behavior is testable per-candidate, including for
579	    candidates that aren't in the default ladder (e.g. ``GLM``, ``QWEN``).
580	    """
581	    family = (
582	        author_family if author_family is not None else resolve_author_family(inputs.author_model, inputs.author_family)
583	    )
584	    normalized_snapshot = normalize_routing_snapshot(inputs.routing_snapshot)
585	    health = _health_of(candidate, normalized_snapshot)
586	    same_family = candidate.family == family
587	
588	    if same_family and family in candidate.advisory_only_for_author_families:
589	        return CandidateResult(
590	            name=candidate.name,
591	            concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
592	            family=candidate.family,
593	            route=candidate.route,
594	            transport=candidate.transport,
595	            invocation=candidate.invocation,
596	            quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
597	            requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
598	            status="advisory_only",
599	            reason=f"same family as author ({family}) — advisory-only, not a formal cross-family gate",
600	            health=health,
601	        )
602	    if same_family:
603	        return CandidateResult(
604	            name=candidate.name,
605	            concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
606	            family=candidate.family,
607	            route=candidate.route,
608	            transport=candidate.transport,
609	            invocation=candidate.invocation,
610	            quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
611	            requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
612	            status="excluded",
613	            reason=f"same family as author ({family}) — cross-family review requires a different family",
614	            health=health,
615	        )
616	
617	    reason = _hard_exclusion_reason(candidate, inputs)
618	    if reason:
619	        return CandidateResult(
620	            name=candidate.name,
621	            concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
622	            family=candidate.family,
623	            route=candidate.route,
624	            transport=candidate.transport,
625	            invocation=candidate.invocation,
626	            quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
627	            requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
628	            status="excluded",
629	            reason=reason,
630	            health=health,
631	        )
632	    circuit_reason = circuit_exclusion_reason(candidate, inputs.routing_snapshot)
633	    if circuit_reason:
634	        return CandidateResult(
635	            name=candidate.name,
636	            concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
637	            family=candidate.family,
638	            route=candidate.route,
639	            transport=candidate.transport,
640	            invocation=candidate.invocation,
641	            quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
642	            requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
643	            status="excluded",
644	            reason=circuit_reason,
645	            health=health,
646	        )
647	    if health == "unhealthy":
648	        return CandidateResult(
649	            name=candidate.name,
650	            concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
651	            family=candidate.family,
652	            route=candidate.route,
653	            transport=candidate.transport,
654	            invocation=candidate.invocation,
655	            quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
656	            requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
657	            status="excluded",
658	            reason="lane health is unhealthy — route is operationally unavailable",
659	            health=health,
660	        )
661	    if health == "near_cap" and inputs.pinned_candidate != candidate.name:
662	        return CandidateResult(
663	            name=candidate.name,
664	            concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
665	            family=candidate.family,
666	            route=candidate.route,
667	            transport=candidate.transport,
668	            invocation=candidate.invocation,
669	            quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
670	            requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
671	            status="excluded",
672	            reason="quota bucket is near cap — automatic assignments are prohibited",
673	            health=health,
674	        )
675	
676	    suitability_rank = _suitability_rank(candidate, inputs)
677	    if suitability_rank is None:
678	        requested = inputs.requested_role or f"{inputs.review_profile}/{inputs.risk} catalog suitability"
679	        return CandidateResult(
680	            name=candidate.name,
681	            concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
682	            family=candidate.family,
683	            route=candidate.route,
684	            transport=candidate.transport,
685	            invocation=candidate.invocation,
686	            quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
687	            requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
688	            status="excluded",
689	            reason=f"missing required review role suitability: {requested}",
690	            health=health,
691	        )
692	
693	    return CandidateResult(
694	        name=candidate.name,
695	        concrete_model=candidate.concrete_model,
696	        family=candidate.family,
697	        route=candidate.route,
698	        transport=candidate.transport,
699	        invocation=candidate.invocation,
700	        quality_tier=candidate.quality_tier,
701	        requires_silence_timeout=candidate.requires_silence_timeout,
702	        status="eligible",
703	        reason=None,
704	        health=health,
705	        suitability_rank=suitability_rank,
706	    )

709	def resolve_reviewer(
710	    inputs: ResolverInputs,
711	    ladder: tuple[tuple[ReviewerCandidate, ...], ...] | None = None,
712	    *,
713	    runtime_state: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
714	    excluded_quota_buckets: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
715	) -> ReviewerResolution:
716	    """Apply hard policy then balance the best eligible quality tier.
717	
718	    Advisory-only candidates
719	    (e.g. ``openai_frontier`` for an OpenAI-family author) are always
720	    surfaced separately, regardless of which rung is selected.
721	
722	    Fails closed — no candidate walked, ``selected`` stays ``None`` — when
723	    the author's model family cannot be resolved to a concrete family (an
724	    unrecognized identity, a bare ambiguous-model harness with no
725	    disambiguation, or a conflicting override). See
726	    :func:`resolve_author_family`.
727	    """
728	    if runtime_state is not None:
729	        # The state owner injects a transaction-consistent snapshot. This
730	        # module never reads a database or service to fill it in.
731	        inputs = replace(inputs, routing_snapshot=runtime_state)
732	    risk = (inputs.risk or "").strip().lower()
733	    review_profile = (inputs.review_profile or "").strip().casefold()
734	    if review_profile not in VALID_REVIEW_PROFILES:
735	        return ReviewerResolution(
736	            selected=None,
737	            advisory=(),
738	            trace=(),
739	            substitution_note=None,
740	            REDACTED,
741	            catalog_reviewed_on=_MODEL_CATALOG["reviewed_on"],
742	            resolved_risk=risk,
743	            fail_closed_reason=(
744	                f"unsupported local-code-review profile {inputs.review_profile!r}; "
745	                f"expected one of {sorted(VALID_REVIEW_PROFILES)}. Learner-content semantic "
746	                "review belongs to track-completion via post-build-review."
747	            ),
748	        )
749	    inputs = replace(inputs, review_profile=review_profile)
750	    if ladder is None and risk not in VALID_RISKS:
751	        return ReviewerResolution(
752	            selected=None,
753	            advisory=(),
754	            trace=(),
755	            substitution_note=None,
756	            REDACTED,
757	            catalog_reviewed_on=_MODEL_CATALOG["reviewed_on"],
758	            resolved_risk=risk,
759	            fail_closed_reason=(f"unsupported review risk {inputs.risk!r}; expected one of {sorted(VALID_RISKS)}"),
760	        )
761	    active_ladder = ladder if ladder is not None else REVIEW_LADDERS[risk]
762	    if inputs.pinned_candidate:
763	        pinned_definition = REVIEW_CANDIDATES.get(inputs.pinned_candidate)
764	        if pinned_definition is None:
765	            return ReviewerResolution(
766	                selected=None,
767	                advisory=(),
768	                trace=(),
769	                substitution_note=None,
770	                REDACTED,
771	                catalog_reviewed_on=_MODEL_CATALOG["reviewed_on"],
772	                resolved_risk=risk,
773	                fail_closed_reason=f"unknown explicit reviewer pin {inputs.pinned_candidate!r}",
774	            )
775	        if all(
776	            candidate.name != pinned_definition.name
777	            for rung in active_ladder
778	            for candidate in rung
779	        ):
780	            # Ladders express automatic preference, not an allowlist.  An
781	            # operator-requested canonical pin may name another catalogued
782	            # candidate, but it still goes through every hard eligibility,
783	            # suitability, isolation, capability, family, health, and circuit
784	            # gate below before it can be selected.
785	            active_ladder = (*active_ladder, (pinned_definition,))
786	    try:
787	        normalize_routing_snapshot(inputs.routing_snapshot)
788	    except ValueError as exc:
789	        return ReviewerResolution(
790	            selected=None,
791	            advisory=(),
792	            trace=(),
793	            substitution_note=None,
794	            REDACTED,
795	            catalog_reviewed_on=_MODEL_CATALOG["reviewed_on"],
796	            resolved_risk=risk,
797	            fail_closed_reason=f"invalid routing snapshot: {exc}",
798	        )
799	
800	    author_family = resolve_author_family(inputs.author_model, inputs.author_family)
801	    if author_family in UNRESOLVED_AUTHOR_FAMILIES:
802	        reason = {
803	            UNKNOWN_AUTHOR_FAMILY: (
804	                f"author identity unknown — cannot resolve a model family from author_model={inputs.author_model!r}"
805	            ),
806	            AMBIGUOUS_AUTHOR_FAMILY: (
807	                f"author harness is multi-model and ambiguous (author_model={inputs.author_model!r}) — "
808	                "supply a concrete author model (e.g. 'cursor:gpt-5.6-sol') or a validated author_family override"
809	            ),
810	            CONFLICTING_AUTHOR_FAMILY: (
811	                f"author identity conflict — the model embedded in author_model={inputs.author_model!r} "
812	                f"disagrees with the declared author_family={inputs.author_family!r} override"
813	            ),
814	        }[author_family]
815	        return ReviewerResolution(
816	            selected=None,
817	            advisory=(),
818	            trace=(),
819	            substitution_note=None,
820	            REDACTED,
821	            catalog_reviewed_on=_MODEL_CATALOG["reviewed_on"],
822	            resolved_risk=risk,
823	            fail_closed_reason=reason,
824	        )
825	
826	    if inputs.pinned_candidate and not (inputs.pressure_override_reason or "").strip():
827	        return ReviewerResolution(
828	            selected=None,
829	            advisory=(),
830	            trace=(),
831	            substitution_note=None,
832	            REDACTED,
833	            catalog_reviewed_on=_MODEL_CATALOG["reviewed_on"],
834	            resolved_risk=risk,
835	            fail_closed_reason="explicit reviewer pin requires a non-empty pressure_override_reason",
836	        )
837	
838	    trace: list[CandidateResult] = []
839	    advisory: list[CandidateResult] = []
840	    selected: CandidateResult | None = None
841	    selected_rung_index: int | None = None
842	    # A ladder orders fallbacks, not traffic. Candidates in separate YAML
843	    # rungs with the same semantic suitability and catalog tier form one
844	    # balancing set, so insertion order cannot pin traffic or promote an idle
845	    # weaker model over a better task fit.
846	    eligible_by_fit_and_tier: dict[tuple[int, int], list[tuple[ReviewerCandidate, CandidateResult, int]]] = {}
847	    tier_for_candidate = {
848	        name: _MODEL_CATALOG["quality_tiers"][candidate.quality_tier]
849	        for name, candidate in REVIEW_CANDIDATES.items()
850	    }
851	
852	    for rung_index, rung in enumerate(active_ladder):
853	        for candidate in rung:
854	            result = evaluate_candidate(candidate, inputs, author_family=author_family)
855	            if result.status == "eligible" and candidate.quota_bucket in excluded_quota_buckets:
856	                result = replace(
857	                    result,
858	                    status="excluded",
859	                    reason=(

259	def _cmd_check_expansion(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:

263	    has no committed endpoint by definition. Every other mode (commit/branch/
264	    pr) is frozen against a committed base/head, so a clean working tree

270	    mode the baseline was actually frozen under.

68	def normalize_line_endings(text: str) -> str:
69	    """Documented normalization: CRLF/CR → LF only. Nothing else."""
70	    return text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

73	def split_lines_preserve_content(text: str) -> list[str]:
74	    """Split on LF after line-ending normalization. Keep empty lines; no strip."""
75	    normalized = normalize_line_endings(text)
76	    if normalized == "":
77	        return []
78	    # splitlines(keepends=False) drops a trailing empty segment after final \n,
79	    # which matches how editors present "lines of a file."
80	    if normalized.endswith("\n"):
81	        normalized = normalized[:-1]
82	    return normalized.split("\n")

85	def is_safe_repo_relative_path(path: str) -> bool:
86	    """Structural path-string check (no filesystem I/O)."""
87	    if not path or not isinstance(path, str):
88	        return False
89	    if path.startswith(("/", "\\")):
90	        return False
91	    if _DRIVE_PATH_RE.match(path):
92	        return False
93	    if "\\" in path:
94	        return False
95	    parts = path.split("/")
96	    return not any(p in ("", ".", "..") for p in parts)

99	def resolve_safe_path(repo_root: Path, rel_path: str) -> Path:
100	    """Resolve ``rel_path`` under ``repo_root``; reject escapes and symlink walks out."""
101	    if not is_safe_repo_relative_path(rel_path):
102	        raise EvidenceError(f"unsafe_path:{rel_path!r}")
103	    root = repo_root.resolve()
104	    candidate = (root / rel_path).resolve(strict=False)
105	    try:
106	        candidate.relative_to(root)
107	    except ValueError as exc:
108	        raise EvidenceError(f"path_escapes_repo:{rel_path!r}") from exc
109	    # If the path exists and is a symlink, ensure the real file is still in-repo.
110	    if candidate.exists() or candidate.is_symlink():
111	        real = candidate.resolve(strict=False)
112	        try:
113	            real.relative_to(root)
114	        except ValueError as exc:
115	            raise EvidenceError(f"symlink_escape:{rel_path!r}") from exc
116	        return real
117	    return candidate

166	def _parse_new_side_lines(diff_text: str) -> set[int]:
167	    """Parse ``git diff -U0`` unified diff for new-side line numbers."""
168	    lines: set[int] = set()
169	    current: int | None = None
170	    remaining = 0
171	    for raw in diff_text.splitlines():
172	        hunk = _HUNK_RE.match(raw)
173	        if hunk:
174	            start = int(hunk.group(1))
175	            count = int(hunk.group(2) or "1")
176	            current = start
177	            remaining = count
178	            if count == 0:
179	                current = None
180	            continue
181	        if current is None:
182	            continue
183	        if raw.startswith("+") and not raw.startswith("+++"):
184	            lines.add(current)
185	            current += 1
186	            remaining -= 1
187	            if remaining <= 0:
188	                current = None
189	        elif (raw.startswith("-") and not raw.startswith("---")) or raw.startswith("\\"):
190	            continue
191	        else:
192	            # context (shouldn't appear with -U0) or noise
193	            if remaining > 0 and not raw.startswith(("+", "-", "@")):
194	                current += 1
195	                remaining -= 1
196	                if remaining <= 0:
197	                    current = None
198	    return lines

201	def changed_lines_map(repo_root: Path, target: ReviewTarget) -> dict[str, set[int]]:
202	    """Map each changed path to the set of new-side line numbers introduced/altered.
203	
204	    Untracked files in local mode: every line is treated as changed.
205	    """
206	    result: dict[str, set[int]] = {p: set() for p in target.changed_paths}
207	    if target.mode == "local":
208	        for path in target.changed_paths:
209	            full = resolve_safe_path(repo_root, path)
210	            # Untracked?
211	            status = _run_git(["status", "--porcelain", "--", path], repo_root)
212	            status_line = (status.stdout or "").strip()
213	            if status_line.startswith("??"):
214	                if full.is_file():
215	                    try:
216	                        text = full.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
217	                    except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
218	                        # Fail closed for line accounting: empty set means present
219	                        # claims cannot invent a verified changed line.
220	                        result[path] = set()
221	                        continue
222	                    n = len(split_lines_preserve_content(text))
223	                    result[path] = set(range(1, n + 1)) if n else set()
224	                continue
225	            # Tracked working-tree changes (staged + unstaged) vs HEAD.
226	            proc = _run_git(["diff", "-U0", "HEAD", "--", path], repo_root)
227	            result[path] |= _parse_new_side_lines(proc.stdout or "")
228	            cached = _run_git(["diff", "-U0", "--cached", "HEAD", "--", path], repo_root)
229	            result[path] |= _parse_new_side_lines(cached.stdout or "")
230	        return result
231	
232	    if not target.base_sha or not target.head_sha:
233	        raise EvidenceError("target_missing_base_or_head_for_changed_lines")
234	    for path in target.changed_paths:
235	        proc = _run_git(
236	            ["diff", "-U0", target.base_sha, target.head_sha, "--", path],
237	            repo_root,
238	        )
239	        if proc.returncode != 0:
240	            raise EvidenceError(f"diff_failed:{path}:{proc.stderr.strip()}")
241	        result[path] = _parse_new_side_lines(proc.stdout or "")
242	    return result

245	def path_surface_bytes(repo_root: Path, target: ReviewTarget, rel_path: str) -> bytes:
246	    """Exact patch or untracked file bytes for one path on the reviewed surface.
247	
248	    Tracked paths use canonical git-diff arguments (binary + full-index, no
249	    ext-diff/textconv/renames). Untracked local paths hash raw file bytes.
250	    """
251	    if not is_safe_repo_relative_path(rel_path):
252	        raise EvidenceError(f"unsafe_path:{rel_path!r}")
253	    if target.mode == "local":
254	        status = _run_git(["status", "--porcelain", "--", rel_path], repo_root)
255	        status_line = (status.stdout or "").strip()
256	        if status_line.startswith("??"):
257	            safe = resolve_safe_path(repo_root, rel_path)
258	            if not safe.is_file():
259	                raise EvidenceError(f"file_unavailable:{rel_path}")
260	            try:
261	                return safe.read_bytes()
262	            except OSError as exc:
263	                raise EvidenceError(f"read_failed:{rel_path}:{exc}") from exc
264	        # Working tree vs HEAD (staged + unstaged combined), canonical form.
265	        proc = _run_git_bytes(
266	            ["diff", *CANONICAL_DIFF_ARGS, "HEAD", "--", rel_path],
267	            repo_root,
268	        )
269	        if proc.returncode not in (0, 1):
270	            err = (proc.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
271	            raise EvidenceError(f"diff_failed:{rel_path}:{err}")
272	        return proc.stdout or b""
273	
274	    if not target.base_sha or not target.head_sha:
275	        raise EvidenceError("target_missing_base_or_head_for_fingerprint")
276	    proc = _run_git_bytes(
277	        [
278	            "diff",
279	            *CANONICAL_DIFF_ARGS,
280	            target.base_sha,
281	            target.head_sha,
282	            "--",
283	            rel_path,
284	        ],
285	        repo_root,
286	    )
287	    if proc.returncode not in (0, 1):
288	        err = (proc.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
289	        raise EvidenceError(f"diff_failed:{rel_path}:{err}")
290	    return proc.stdout or b""

293	def compute_target_input_fingerprint(repo_root: Path, target: ReviewTarget) -> str:
294	    """Deterministic SHA-256 of target metadata plus exact patch/untracked bytes.
295	
296	    Identifies the validated review target/bundle (not reviewer JSON). Changes
297	    when local sources, the changed-path set, base/head, or committed content
298	    change.
299	    """
300	    working_tree_head = ""
301	    if target.mode == "local":
302	        head_proc = _run_git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], repo_root)
303	        if head_proc.returncode == 0:
304	            working_tree_head = (head_proc.stdout or "").strip()
305	
306	    # ``description`` is display-only and may contain the caller's ref spelling
307	    # (for example ``HEAD`` versus a branch name).  Binding it would give the
308	    # same immutable target different fingerprints depending on how it was
309	    # addressed, so only stable target identity belongs in the hash.
310	    meta = {
311	        "fingerprint_version": TARGET_INPUT_FINGERPRINT_VERSION,
312	        "mode": target.mode,
313	        "base_sha": target.base_sha or "",
314	        "head_sha": target.head_sha or "",
315	        "working_tree_head": working_tree_head,
316	        "changed_paths": list(target.changed_paths),
317	        "non_test_loc": target.non_test_loc,
318	        "clean_tree": target.clean_tree,
319	    }
320	    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
321	    hasher.update(TARGET_INPUT_FINGERPRINT_VERSION.encode("utf-8"))
322	    hasher.update(b"\0")
323	    hasher.update(
324	        json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode(
325	            "utf-8"
326	        )
327	    )
328	    for path in target.changed_paths:
329	        surface = path_surface_bytes(repo_root, target, path)
330	        hasher.update(b"\0path:")
331	        hasher.update(path.encode("utf-8"))
332	        hasher.update(b"\0len:")
333	        hasher.update(f"{len(surface)}".encode("ascii"))
334	        hasher.update(b"\0")
335	        hasher.update(surface)
336	    return hasher.hexdigest()

339	def build_target_manifest(repo_root: Path, target: ReviewTarget) -> dict:
340	    """Source-blind capture of head + target-input fingerprint before review."""
341	    input_sha256 = compute_target_input_fingerprint(repo_root, target)
342	    return {
343	        "schema_version": "code-review-target-manifest.v1",
344	        "mode": target.mode,
345	        "base_sha": target.base_sha,
346	        "head_sha": target.head_sha,
347	        "changed_paths": list(target.changed_paths),
348	        "non_test_loc": target.non_test_loc,
349	        "clean_tree": target.clean_tree,

355	def find_verbatim_match(
356	    file_text: str, quote: str
357	) -> tuple[int | None, str | None]:
358	    """Return (1-based start line, matched text) of the first contiguous match.
359	
360	    Matching uses line-ending normalization only. First match is deterministic
361	    for reporting an alternate location when the claimed range does not match.
362	    """
363	    file_lines = split_lines_preserve_content(file_text)
364	    quote_lines = split_lines_preserve_content(quote)
365	    if not quote_lines:
366	        return None, None
367	    n = len(quote_lines)
368	    for i in range(0, len(file_lines) - n + 1):
369	        window = file_lines[i : i + n]
370	        if window == quote_lines:
371	            matched = "\n".join(window)
372	            return i + 1, matched
373	    return None, None
374	
375	
376	def match_at_line(file_text: str, quote: str, start_line: int) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
377	    """True if ``quote`` matches contiguously starting at 1-based ``start_line``."""
378	    file_lines = split_lines_preserve_content(file_text)
379	    quote_lines = split_lines_preserve_content(quote)
380	    if not quote_lines or start_line < 1:
381	        return False, None
382	    idx = start_line - 1
383	    end = idx + len(quote_lines)
384	    if end > len(file_lines):
385	        return False, None
386	    window = file_lines[idx:end]
387	    if window != quote_lines:
388	        return False, None
389	    return True, "\n".join(window)
390	
391	
392	def expected_end_line_for_quote(start_line: int, quote: str) -> int:
393	    """Inclusive end_line that exactly covers the verbatim span."""
394	    n = len(split_lines_preserve_content(quote))
395	    if n < 1:
396	        return start_line
397	    return start_line + n - 1

400	def verify_finding_evidence(
401	    finding: dict,
402	    *,
403	    repo_root: Path,
404	    target: ReviewTarget,
405	    changed_lines: dict[str, set[int]],
406	) -> EvidenceCheckResult:
407	    """Validate one schema-valid finding against the frozen target."""
408	    location = finding.get("location") or {}
409	    path = location.get("path")
410	    start_line = location.get("start_line")
411	    end_line = location.get("end_line")
412	    claim_type = location.get("claim_type")
413	    verbatim = finding.get("verbatim")
414	
415	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not is_safe_repo_relative_path(path):
416	        return EvidenceCheckResult(OUTCOME_MALFORMED, detail="unsafe_or_invalid_path")
417	    if not isinstance(start_line, int) or not isinstance(end_line, int):
418	        return EvidenceCheckResult(OUTCOME_MALFORMED, detail="invalid_line_types")
419	    if start_line < 1 or end_line < start_line:
420	        return EvidenceCheckResult(OUTCOME_MALFORMED, detail="invalid_line_range")
421	    if claim_type not in ("present", "missing"):
422	        return EvidenceCheckResult(OUTCOME_MALFORMED, detail="invalid_claim_type")
423	    if not isinstance(verbatim, str) or not verbatim:
424	        return EvidenceCheckResult(OUTCOME_MALFORMED, detail="empty_verbatim")
425	
426	    try:
427	        resolve_safe_path(repo_root, path)
428	    except EvidenceError as exc:
429	        return EvidenceCheckResult(OUTCOME_MALFORMED, detail=str(exc))
430	
431	    if path not in target.changed_paths:
432	        return EvidenceCheckResult(
433	            OUTCOME_OUT_OF_SCOPE,
434	            detail=f"path_not_in_changed_paths:{path}",
435	        )
436	
437	    try:
438	        file_text = load_file_text(repo_root, path, target)
439	    except EvidenceError as exc:
440	        return EvidenceCheckResult(OUTCOME_QUOTE_MISSING, detail=str(exc))
441	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
442	        return EvidenceCheckResult(
443	            OUTCOME_QUOTE_MISSING,
444	            detail=f"read_or_decode_failed:{path}:{exc}",
445	        )
446	
447	    quote_lines = split_lines_preserve_content(verbatim)
448	    expected_end = expected_end_line_for_quote(start_line, verbatim)
449	    alternate_line, alternate_text = find_verbatim_match(file_text, verbatim)
450	
451	    # Range must equal the exact verbatim span (blocks inflated ranges that
452	    # intersect unrelated changed lines).
453	    if end_line != expected_end:
454	        return EvidenceCheckResult(
455	            OUTCOME_LINE_MISMATCH,
456	            matched_line=alternate_line,
457	            matched_text=alternate_text,
458	            detail=(
459	                f"range_span_mismatch:claimed={start_line}-{end_line} "
460	                f"expected_end={expected_end} quote_lines={len(quote_lines)}"
461	                + (f" actual_match_at={alternate_line}" if alternate_line is not None else "")
462	            ),
463	        )
464	
465	    at_claim, matched_text = match_at_line(file_text, verbatim, start_line)
466	    if at_claim:
467	        matched_line = start_line
468	    else:
469	        if alternate_line is None:
470	            return EvidenceCheckResult(
471	                OUTCOME_QUOTE_MISSING,
472	                detail="verbatim_not_found",
473	            )
474	        return EvidenceCheckResult(
475	            OUTCOME_LINE_MISMATCH,
476	            matched_line=alternate_line,
477	            matched_text=alternate_text,
478	            detail=f"matched_at_line:{alternate_line}",
479	        )
480	
481	    path_changed = changed_lines.get(path, set())
482	    primary_lines = set(range(start_line, end_line + 1))
483	    # present: primary location must land on a changed line.
484	    # missing: contextual evidence may sit on an unchanged line; do not invent
485	    # a diff line for the absent code.
486	    if claim_type == "present" and not primary_lines & path_changed:
487	        return EvidenceCheckResult(
488	            OUTCOME_OUT_OF_SCOPE,
489	            matched_line=matched_line,
490	            matched_text=matched_text,
491	            detail=(
492	                f"primary_location_not_on_changed_line:"
493	                f"{path}:{start_line}-{end_line}"
494	            ),
495	        )
496	
497	    return EvidenceCheckResult(
498	        OUTCOME_VERIFIED,
499	        matched_line=matched_line,
500	        matched_text=matched_text,
501	        detail=f"matched_at_line:{matched_line}",
502	    )

95	def _canonical_review_response_text(response: str) -> str:
96	    """Extract one JSON object from the two bounded ACP wrapper shapes."""
97	    stripped = response.strip()
98	    match = re.fullmatch(r"```json\r?\n(?P<body>.+)\r?\n```", stripped, re.DOTALL)
99	    if match is not None and "```" not in match.group("body"):
100	        return match.group("body").strip()
101	    wrapped_match = re.fullmatch(
102	        r"(?P<prefix>.{1,500}?)\r?\n```json\r?\n(?P<body>.+)\r?\n```",
103	        stripped,
104	        re.DOTALL,
105	    )
106	    if wrapped_match is not None:
107	        prefix = wrapped_match.group("prefix")
108	        # Admit the common provider wrapper only when it is bounded prose,
109	        # followed by exactly one terminal JSON fence. Schema validation still
110	        # owns the verdict; this merely normalizes transport decoration.
111	        body = wrapped_match.group("body")
112	        if (
113	            "{" not in prefix
114	            and "}" not in prefix
115	            and "```" not in prefix
116	            and "```" not in body
117	        ):
118	            return body.strip()
119	    object_start = stripped.find("{")
120	    if object_start > 0 and "}" not in stripped[:object_start]:
121	        try:
122	            _value, object_end = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(stripped, object_start)

130	def _normalize_known_null_review_annotations(response: str) -> str:
131	    """Remove only known null provider annotations from finding objects.
132	
133	    The canonical schema remains strict: non-null annotations, unrelated extra
134	    fields, duplicate JSON keys, and malformed responses are returned unchanged
135	    so the normal validator can reject them.
136	    """
137	
138	    def _reject_duplicate_keys(pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
139	        value: dict[str, Any] = {}
140	        for key, item in pairs:
141	            if key in value:
142	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate JSON key: {key}")
143	            value[key] = item
144	        return value
145	
146	    try:
147	        payload = json.loads(response, object_pairs_hook=_reject_duplicate_keys)
148	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
149	        return response
150	    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not isinstance(payload.get("findings"), list):
151	        return response
152	
153	    changed = False
154	    for finding in payload["findings"]:
155	        if (
156	            isinstance(finding, dict)
157	            and "verbatim_note" in finding
158	            and finding["verbatim_note"] is None
159	        ):
160	            del finding["verbatim_note"]
161	            changed = True
162	    if not changed:
163	        return response
164	    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))

235	def _compute_review_routing_budget() -> dict[str, Any]:
236	    """Take a bounded fresh capacity snapshot for this standalone process."""
237	    from scripts.api.codexbar_usage import refresh_provider_usage_data
238	    from scripts.api.state_router import SUBSCRIPTION_LANES, compute_routing_budget
239	
240	    # CodexBar's last-known-good cache is process-local. A new review-pr
241	    # process therefore cannot use cache-only mode without falsely marking
242	    # every subscription lane unavailable and draining the API-backed lanes.
243	    budget = compute_routing_budget(fresh_codexbar=True)
244	    agents = budget.get("agents") if isinstance(budget, dict) else None
245	    unavailable = tuple(
246	        lane
247	        for lane in SUBSCRIPTION_LANES
248	        if isinstance(agents, dict)
249	        and isinstance(agents.get(lane), dict)
250	        and agents[lane].get("status") in {"unknown", "unavailable"}
251	    )
252	    if unavailable:
253	        # Retry missing lanes one at a time rather than one more all-lane
254	        # refresh. Uses the shared realistic timeout floor (25s default,
255	        # CODEXBAR_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_S) — the prior 5.0s override was still
256	        # shorter than the claude lane's live-measured ~17s CLI latency and
257	        # reproduced the same false-'unavailable' misclassification.
258	        for lane in unavailable:
259	            refresh_provider_usage_data((lane,))
260	        # The retry populated this process's last-known-good cache; do not
261	        # launch a second all-provider refresh while projecting it.
262	        budget = compute_routing_budget(fresh_codexbar=False)
263	    return budget

393	def resolve_requested_review_candidate(
394	    reviewer_request: str,
395	    explicit_model: str | None,
396	    candidates: Mapping[str, Any],
397	) -> str | None:
398	    """Resolve one explicit request without confusing a route with its default.
399	
400	    ``--reviewer`` names a semantic/native route, while ``--model`` may select
401	    any formally eligible canonical candidate on that route.  The default
402	    candidate remains authoritative when no model is supplied.  Model-only
403	    requests consider formally eligible candidates only, which disambiguates
404	    an attested native route from a non-formal fallback carrying the same model.
405	    """
406	    model = (explicit_model or "").strip() or None
407	    default_name = None
408	    requested_route = None
409	    if reviewer_request != REVIEWER_AUTO:
410	        default_name = EXPLICIT_REVIEWER_CANDIDATE[reviewer_request]
411	        try:
412	            requested_route = candidates[default_name].route
413	        except (KeyError, AttributeError) as exc:
414	            raise ReviewSafetyError(
415	                f"reviewer_catalog_mismatch: default candidate {default_name!r} "
416	                f"for reviewer {reviewer_request!r} is unavailable"
417	            ) from exc
418	        if not candidates[default_name].formal_review_eligible:
419	            reason = candidates[default_name].formal_review_exclusion_reason or "sealed endpoint is not eligible"
420	            raise ReviewSafetyError(
421	                f"reviewer_not_formal_review_eligible: {reviewer_request!r} cannot satisfy "
422	                f"the formal review gate: {reason}"
423	            )
424	        if model is None:
425	            return default_name
426	    elif model is None:
427	        return None
428	
429	    matches = [
430	        candidate.name
431	        for candidate in candidates.values()
432	        if candidate.concrete_model == model
433	        and candidate.formal_review_eligible
434	        and (requested_route is None or candidate.route == requested_route)
435	    ]
436	    if len(matches) == 1:
437	        return matches[0]
438	
439	    if requested_route is None:
440	        scope = "the formal-review catalog"
441	        eligible_models = sorted(
442	            {
443	                candidate.concrete_model
444	                for candidate in candidates.values()
445	                if candidate.formal_review_eligible
446	            }
447	        )
448	    else:
449	        scope = f"reviewer {reviewer_request!r} route {requested_route!r}"
450	        eligible_models = sorted(
451	            {
452	                candidate.concrete_model
453	                for candidate in candidates.values()
454	                if candidate.formal_review_eligible and candidate.route == requested_route
455	            }
456	        )
457	    if not matches:
458	        raise ReviewSafetyError(
459	            f"model_not_formal_review_eligible: {model!r} has no canonical candidate on {scope}; "
460	            f"eligible models: {eligible_models!r}"
461	        )
462	    if requested_route is None:
463	        ambiguity_advice = "add --reviewer to select the native route"
464	    else:
465	        ambiguity_advice = (
466	            f"route {requested_route!r} defines duplicate canonical candidates for this model; "
467	            "disambiguate scripts/config/model_catalog.yaml"
468	        )
469	    raise ReviewSafetyError(
470	        f"ambiguous_formal_review_model: {model!r} maps to candidates {sorted(matches)!r} on {scope}; "
471	        f"{ambiguity_advice}"
472	    )

505	def _codex_read_calls(
506	    checkout: review_worktree.ProvisionedReviewWorktree,
507	) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
508	    calls: list[dict[str, object]] = []
509	    required = review_worktree._required_review_read_paths(
510	        checkout.path,
511	        checkout.changed_paths,
512	    )
513	    for rel_path in required:
514	        data = (checkout.path / rel_path).read_bytes()
515	        offsets = range(0, max(1, len(data)), 64 * 1024)
516	        for offset in offsets:
517	            chunk = data[offset : offset + 64 * 1024]
518	            next_offset = offset + len(chunk)
519	            payload = {
520	                "path": rel_path,
521	                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
522	                "offset": offset,
523	                "chunk_bytes": len(chunk),
524	                "chunk_sha256": hashlib.sha256(chunk).hexdigest(),
525	                "next_offset": next_offset,
526	                "total_bytes": len(data),
527	                "eof": next_offset == len(data),
528	                "content": chunk.decode("utf-8"),
529	            }
530	            calls.append(
531	                {
532	                    "name": "mcp__sealed_review__read_file",
533	                    "arguments": {"path": rel_path, "offset": offset, "max_bytes": 64 * 1024},
534	                    "result": {
535	                        "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(payload)}],
536	                        "isError": False,
537	                    },
538	                }
539	            )
540	    return calls

612	    checkout: review_worktree.ProvisionedReviewWorktree,
613	) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
614	    direct_calls = _codex_read_calls(checkout)
615	    required = review_worktree._required_review_read_paths(checkout.path, checkout.changed_paths)
616	    calls: list[dict[str, object]] = []
617	    for start in range(0, len(direct_calls), review_worktree.MAX_CODEX_REQUIRED_READ_CHUNKS):
618	        batch = direct_calls[start : start + review_worktree.MAX_CODEX_REQUIRED_READ_CHUNKS]
619	        first_arguments = batch[0]["arguments"]
620	        assert isinstance(first_arguments, dict)
621	        start_index = required.index(first_arguments["path"])
622	        start_offset = first_arguments["offset"]
623	        chunks: list[dict[str, object]] = []
624	        next_index = start_index
625	        next_offset = start_offset
626	        for direct in batch:
627	            wrapped = direct["result"]
628	            assert isinstance(wrapped, dict)
629	            content = wrapped["content"]
630	            assert isinstance(content, list)
631	            payload = json.loads(content[0]["text"])
632	            chunks.append(payload)
633	            path_index = required.index(payload["path"])
634	            if payload["eof"]:
635	                next_index = path_index + 1
636	                next_offset = 0
637	            else:
638	                next_index = path_index
639	                next_offset = payload["next_offset"]
640	        outer_payload = {
641	            "index": start_index,
642	            "offset": start_offset,
643	            "next_index": next_index,
644	            "next_offset": next_offset,
645	            "required_path_count": len(required),
646	            "eof": next_index == len(required),
647	            "chunks": chunks,
648	        }

650	            "content": [

669	                        "type": "input_text",

673	                        "type": "input_text",

def test_validate_code_review_response_normalizes_endpoint_only_mismatch(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Reproduce #6415 item 2: quoted lines match but claimed end is off-by-one.

    The validator must accept an endpoint-only mismatch when the verbatim quote
    matches the file text exactly at the claimed start line. Wrong quoted content
    must still fail closed.
    """
    base = "b" * 40
    head = "a" * 40
    patch = "c" * 64
    evidence_root = tmp_path / "evidence"

    (evidence_root / "src" / "app.py").write_text(
        "line1\nline2\nline3\nline4\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    changed_lines = {"src/app.py": frozenset({1, 2, 3, 4})}

    def _finding(verbatim: str, start_line: int, end_line: int) -> dict:
        return {
            "schema_version": "code-review-findings.v1",
            "overall": {

                "explanation": "One actionable defect was found.",
                "confidence": 0.95,
            },
            "findings": [
                {
                    "id": "F001",
                    "title": "Example finding",
                    "body": "The exact changed lines are incorrect.",
                    "priority": "P1",
                    "confidence": 0.95,
                    "category": "correctness",
                    "location": {
                        "path": "src/app.py",
                        "start_line": start_line,
                        "end_line": end_line,
                        "claim_type": "present",
                    },
                    "verbatim": verbatim,
                    "why_wrong": "The values produce the wrong behavior.",
                    "smallest_fix": "Correct the changed lines.",
                    "sources": ["none"],
                }
            ],
        }

    # Observed failure shape from acpx-claude-shadow: 4-line verbatim, claimed
    # end is one less than the inclusive span (start + quote_lines - 1).
    short_end = _finding("line1\nline2\nline3\nline4", 1, 3)
    digest = review_worktree.validate_code_review_response(
        json.dumps(short_end),
        base_sha=base,
        head_sha=head,
        patch_sha256=patch,
        changed_paths=("src/app.py",),
        evidence_root=evidence_root,
        changed_lines=changed_lines,

        base_sha=base,
        head_sha=head,
        patch_sha256=patch,
        changed_paths=("src/app.py",),
        evidence_root=evidence_root,
        changed_lines=changed_lines,
    )
    assert len(digest) == 64

    # Mutation: wrong quoted content must still fail, even when the claimed
    # range equals the verbatim length.
    wrong_content = _finding("line1\nWRONG\nline3\nline4", 1, 4)
    with pytest.raises(review_worktree.ReviewWorktreeError, match="review_response_evidence"):

def _cmd_list_eligible(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Print every seat's eligibility for the given author identity.

    Runs the same resolver used by the formal review scheduler, but performs no
    provisioning, authority, or routing side effects.
    """
    from scripts.review.reviewer_resolver import ResolverInputs, resolve_reviewer

    author_model = str(getattr(args, "author_model", None) or "").strip()
    author_family = str(getattr(args, "author_family", None) or "").strip()
    if not author_model or not author_family:
        print(
            "review-pr: concrete_author_identity_required: pass --author-model and --author-family",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    routing_snapshot = None
    routing_snapshot_file = getattr(args, "routing_snapshot_file", None)
    if routing_snapshot_file:
        routing_snapshot = json.loads(Path(routing_snapshot_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    profile = str(getattr(args, "review_profile", None) or "code").strip().lower()
    risk = str(getattr(args, "risk", None) or "medium").strip().lower()
    inputs = ResolverInputs(
        author_model=author_model,
        author_family=author_family,
        review_profile=profile,
        risk=risk,
        domain=profile,
        required_capabilities=frozenset(args.required_capability or ()),
        data_egress_policy=args.data_egress_policy,
        isolation_required=bool(getattr(args, "isolation_required", True)),
        routing_snapshot=routing_snapshot,
    )
    resolution = resolve_reviewer(inputs)

    def _candidate_dict(item: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "name": item.name,
            "model": item.concrete_model,
            "family": item.family,
            "route": item.route,
            "status": item.status,
            "reason": item.reason,
            "health": item.health,
            "suitability_rank": item.suitability_rank,
            "quality_tier": item.quality_tier,
        }

    output = {
        "seats": [_candidate_dict(item) for item in resolution.trace],
        "selected": _candidate_dict(resolution.selected) if resolution.selected else None,
        "fail_closed_reason": resolution.fail_closed_reason,
        "policy_version": resolution.policy_version,
        "catalog_reviewed_on": resolution.catalog_reviewed_on,
        "resolved_risk": resolution.resolved_risk,
    }
    print(json.dumps(output, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


def handle_review_pr(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """CLI handler for ``review-pr``."""
    if getattr(args, "list_eligible", False):
        return _cmd_list_eligible(args)

    try:
        pr = parse_pr_number(str(args.pr))
        reviewer_request = resolve_reviewer(args.reviewer, claude_available=args.claude_available)
        initiator = str(
            getattr(args, "initiator", None)
            or getattr(args, "from_llm", None)
            or os.environ.get("SESSION_HANDOFF_AGENT")
            or ""
        ).strip()
        author_model = str(getattr(args, "author_model", None) or "").strip()
        author_family = str(getattr(args, "author_family", None) or "").strip()
        if not initiator:
            raise ReviewSafetyError("initiator_required: pass --initiator")
        if not author_model or not author_family:
            raise ReviewSafetyError("concrete_author_identity_required: pass --author-model and --author-family")
    except ReviewSafetyError as exc:
        print(f"review-pr: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

def _cmd_list_eligible(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Print every seat's eligibility for the given author identity.

    Runs the same resolver used by the formal review scheduler, but performs no
    provisioning, authority, or routing side effects.
    """
    from scripts.review.reviewer_resolver import ResolverInputs, resolve_reviewer

    author_model = str(getattr(args, "author_model", None) or "").strip()
    author_family = str(getattr(args, "author_family", None) or "").strip()
    if not author_model or not author_family:
        print(
            "review-pr: concrete_author_identity_required: pass --author-model and --author-family",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    routing_snapshot = None
    routing_snapshot_file = getattr(args, "routing_snapshot_file", None)
    if routing_snapshot_file:
        routing_snapshot = json.loads(Path(routing_snapshot_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    profile = str(getattr(args, "review_profile", None) or "code").strip().lower()
    risk = str(getattr(args, "risk", None) or "medium").strip().lower()
    inputs = ResolverInputs(
        author_model=author_model,
        author_family=author_family,
        review_profile=profile,
        risk=risk,
        domain=profile,
        required_capabilities=frozenset(args.required_capability or ()),
        data_egress_policy=args.data_egress_policy,
        isolation_required=bool(getattr(args, "isolation_required", True)),
        routing_snapshot=routing_snapshot,
    )
    resolution = resolve_reviewer(inputs)

    def _candidate_dict(item: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "name": item.name,
            "model": item.concrete_model,
            "family": item.family,
            "route": item.route,
            "status": item.status,
            "reason": item.reason,
            "health": item.health,
            "suitability_rank": item.suitability_rank,
            "quality_tier": item.quality_tier,
        }

    output = {
        "seats": [_candidate_dict(item) for item in resolution.trace],
        "selected": _candidate_dict(resolution.selected) if resolution.selected else None,
        "fail_closed_reason": resolution.fail_closed_reason,
        "policy_version": resolution.policy_version,
        "catalog_reviewed_on": resolution.catalog_reviewed_on,
        "resolved_risk": resolution.resolved_risk,
    }
    print(json.dumps(output, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


def handle_review_pr(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """CLI handler for ``review-pr``."""
    if getattr(args, "list_eligible", False):
        return _cmd_list_eligible(args)

    try:
        pr = parse_pr_number(str(args.pr))
        reviewer_request = resolve_reviewer(args.reviewer, claude_available=args.claude_available)
        initiator = str(
            getattr(args, "initiator", None)
            or getattr(args, "from_llm", None)
            or os.environ.get("SESSION_HANDOFF_AGENT")
            or ""
        ).strip()
        author_model = str(getattr(args, "author_model", None) or "").strip()
        author_family = str(getattr(args, "author_family", None) or "").strip()
        if not initiator:
            raise ReviewSafetyError("initiator_required: pass --initiator")
        if not author_model or not author_family:
            raise ReviewSafetyError("concrete_author_identity_required: pass --author-model and --author-family")
    except ReviewSafetyError as exc:
        print(f"review-pr: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
